name: Vacuum Cleaner Motor
definition: A vacuum-cleaner motor profile covers the motor and fan or blower assembly used to create an airflow-pressure operating point for suction; it does not automatically include brush-roll drive motors, appliance controls or an exact replacement part.
includedScope: Universal and brushless suction motor-fan families
Electrical, airflow, pressure, mechanical and protection checks
headline: Motor family, wattage and appearance are starting clues—not compatibility proof.
description: This component profile separates motor architecture, airflow-performance measurements and exact replacement checks so buyers can compare documented boundaries without inventing an OEM or fit relationship.
metaDescription: Vacuum cleaner motor types, airflow and suction specifications, motor-fan families, failure boundaries and exact compatibility checks for procurement and engineering.
disclaimer: Physical resemblance, matching wattage, a generic family name or a seller claim does not establish compatibility. Verify the current manufacturer part number, appliance model and serial scope, electrical and control specification, mechanical and airflow interfaces, protection requirements and approved service documentation.

keyFacts.label: Core output
keyFacts.value: An airflow-pressure operating point created by the motor and fan or blower assembly
keyFacts.evidence: ASTM F2105 covers suction, airflow, air power, maximum air power and input power for vacuum-cleaner motor/fan systems under specified conditions.
keyFacts.scope: Series-universal motor/fan systems within ASTM F2105-21; other architectures require their applicable manufacturer method.

keyFacts.label: Cooling families
keyFacts.value: Thru-flow and bypass are distinct documented arrangements
keyFacts.evidence: Domel lists brushless vacuum motors in thru-flow and bypass versions and separates dry thru-flow from dry/wet bypass product groups.
keyFacts.scope: Domel published product portfolio; not a universal naming rule for every manufacturer.

keyFacts.label: Electrical range
keyFacts.value: Cannot be inferred from package size
keyFacts.evidence: Domel's named brushless families span stated 12–48 V and 12–230 V ranges, while Johnson Electric's U9825-001 datasheet specifies 120 V AC.
keyFacts.scope: Named Domel families and Johnson U9825-001 only.

keyFacts.label: Performance boundary
keyFacts.value: Motor/fan inlet data is not the same as cleaning performance at the floor
keyFacts.evidence: ASTM F2105 compares maximum air power at the motor/fan inlet; IEC 62885-2 addresses whole dry-vacuum performance methods.
keyFacts.scope: The named standards and their stated equipment scopes.

keyFacts.label: Compatibility rule
keyFacts.value: Exact documentation must pass identity, electrical, mechanical, system and safety checks
keyFacts.evidence: Official motor pages and datasheets publish different voltage, architecture, dimensions, control, protection and test-condition fields; IEC and UL references apply additional safety boundaries.
keyFacts.scope: Procurement framework synthesized by WCB from the reviewed fields; not a manufacturer compatibility declaration.

systemRole.name: Electrical input and control
systemRole.role: Supplies the specified AC or DC input and, for electronically commutated designs, the required controller signals and protection.
systemRole.evidence: Domel states multiple voltage versions for battery and corded brushless motors; UL identifies separate rotating-machine and electronically protected motor standards.
systemRole.scope: Reviewed Domel brushless families and UL standards overview.

systemRole.name: Electromagnetic conversion
systemRole.role: The motor converts electrical input into shaft rotation within its stated voltage, load, thermal and control boundary.
systemRole.evidence: Nidec describes high-speed brushless DC motors developed for cordless vacuum cleaners and publishes output ratings for V45, V55 and V65.
systemRole.scope: Nidec cordless-vacuum case study and named lineup.

systemRole.name: Fan or blower stage
systemRole.role: One or more fan stages use shaft power to create airflow and pressure characteristics.
systemRole.evidence: Domel describes universal wet/dry units with one or more fan stages; ASTM F2105 defines measurements for motor/fan systems.
systemRole.scope: Domel bypass product group and ASTM F2105 scope.

systemRole.name: Air path and operating point
systemRole.role: Restriction, fan geometry and system interfaces determine where airflow and pressure operate together.
systemRole.evidence: Johnson Electric reports U9825-001 airflow, vacuum, speed and air-power values at open, 19 mm orifice and sealed conditions.

systemRole.name: Cooling and protection
systemRole.role: Cooling path, insulation and thermal or electronic protection must remain consistent with the approved appliance design.
systemRole.evidence: Domel distinguishes thru-flow and bypass families; UL lists general, thermally protected and electronically protected motor standards.
systemRole.scope: Family-level architecture and standards boundary; no certification is inferred.

architectures.name: Universal commutator motor
architectures.operatingPrinciple: Mechanical commutation through brushes and a commutator drives the motor/fan assembly.
architectures.applicationBoundary: Domel identifies universal commutator motors as the foundation of its vacuum-motor offer; ASTM F2105 specifically covers series-universal motor/fan systems.
benefits: Broad documented AC and low-voltage family coverage
limitations: Brush and commutator wear remain service-life variables
Family data cannot replace exact part data
architectures.buyerCheck: Confirm voltage, fan stage, cooling arrangement, life-test condition, brush system and approved part number.
architectures.evidence: Domel publishes universal vacuum families and ASTM publishes a motor/fan air-performance method for series-universal systems.
architectures.scope: Domel portfolio and ASTM F2105-21 scope.

architectures.name: Brushless DC / EC motor
architectures.operatingPrinciple: Electronic commutation replaces the brush-commutator interface and requires a compatible drive or integrated controller.
architectures.applicationBoundary: Domel lists battery and corded brushless vacuum families; Nidec documents cordless vacuum motors.
benefits: Manufacturers describe compact, efficient and long-life designs
Control can support application-specific operating modes
limitations: Controller, firmware, sensors and wiring become compatibility fields
architectures.buyerCheck: Approve the motor and control system together, including input range, signals, protection and operating point.
architectures.evidence: Domel and Nidec describe electronically commutated vacuum-motor product families and their stated application benefits.
architectures.scope: Named Domel and Nidec families only.

architectures.name: Thru-flow cooling
architectures.operatingPrinciple: Working air passes through or around the motor section as part of the cooling path.
architectures.applicationBoundary: Domel separates thru-flow motors for dry applications and publishes brushless thru-flow families.
benefits: Compact integrated air path in documented dry applications
limitations: The reviewed Domel product grouping limits thru-flow families to dry application context
architectures.buyerCheck: Confirm the exact permitted medium, cooling route, orientation, filters and restriction range.
architectures.evidence: Domel publishes a dedicated thru-flow motors for dry applications group and named brushless thru-flow series.
architectures.scope: Domel product taxonomy; not a universal prohibition for every design.

architectures.name: Bypass cooling
architectures.operatingPrinciple: A separate cooling-air route isolates motor cooling from the working-air stream.
architectures.applicationBoundary: Domel publishes bypass motors for dry and wet applications and brushless bypass series.
benefits: Separate cooling path in the named designs
limitations: Bypass does not alone establish wet-use approval
Seals, discharge orientation and insulation still vary
architectures.buyerCheck: Match dry/wet declaration, discharge geometry, seals, insulation, mounting and exact electrical data.
architectures.evidence: Domel's bypass product group describes dry/wet units and publishes radial or tangential discharge and insulation variants.

specifications.name: Rated voltage and frequency
specifications.purchasingMeaning: Defines the permitted supply boundary and region or battery-system interface.
specifications.reportingBoundary: AC/DC type, voltage range and frequency must remain attached to the exact part.
specifications.comparisonCaution: The same package or family can have multiple voltage versions.
specifications.evidence: Domel publishes 12–48 V and up to 230 V variants; U9825-001 specifies 120 V AC.

specifications.name: Input power
specifications.purchasingMeaning: Electrical power consumed at the declared operating condition.
specifications.reportingBoundary: It is not air power, shaft output or floor pickup.
specifications.comparisonCaution: Do not compare without load point, voltage and test method.
specifications.evidence: ASTM F2105 lists input power separately from suction, airflow and air power.

specifications.name: Airflow
specifications.purchasingMeaning: Volume flow at a stated restriction or opening.
specifications.reportingBoundary: Measurement location and restriction define the value.
specifications.comparisonCaution: Open-flow data cannot be treated as the operating value inside another appliance.
specifications.evidence: U9825-001 publishes airflow at open condition and separate values at defined test points.

specifications.name: Sealed vacuum / static pressure
specifications.purchasingMeaning: Pressure potential near a no-flow condition.
specifications.reportingBoundary: The sealed point is different from a working airflow point.
specifications.comparisonCaution: High sealed vacuum alone does not establish debris pickup or usable airflow.
specifications.evidence: Johnson Electric separates open, orifice and sealed performance conditions.

specifications.name: Air power
specifications.purchasingMeaning: A calculated combination of airflow and pressure at a stated point.
specifications.reportingBoundary: ASTM F2105 locates comparison at the motor/fan system inlet under its method.
specifications.comparisonCaution: It is not input watts and not whole-appliance cleaning performance.
specifications.evidence: ASTM F2105 states that results compare maximum air power at the motor/fan inlet under the method's conditions.

specifications.name: Speed
specifications.purchasingMeaning: Helps define the motor-fan operating point and control requirement.
specifications.reportingBoundary: Speed changes with restriction and control mode.
specifications.comparisonCaution: Higher rpm is not automatically higher usable suction or longer life.
specifications.evidence: Nidec documents approximately 80,000 rpm in a 2016 cordless design; Johnson publishes different U9825-001 speeds at open, orifice and seal.
specifications.scope: Named Nidec development and Johnson datasheet.

specifications.name: Life-test condition
specifications.purchasingMeaning: Shows the duty and restriction boundary behind a stated typical life value.
specifications.reportingBoundary: Cycle, orifice, temperature and load are inseparable from the result.
specifications.comparisonCaution: Hours from different cycles are not directly equivalent.
specifications.evidence: U9825-001 states a typical life and an 8-minute-on / 2-minute-off test condition at a named orifice.
specifications.scope: Johnson Electric U9825-001 only; no field-life prediction.

specifications.name: Envelope, mount and interfaces
specifications.purchasingMeaning: Defines whether the part can be integrated without changing structure, ducting, sealing or wiring.
specifications.reportingBoundary: Diameter and length alone omit mount, fan, discharge, connector and revision details.
specifications.comparisonCaution: Physical resemblance does not establish fit.
specifications.evidence: Official families publish different diameters, voltage ranges, discharge arrangements and electrical connections.
specifications.scope: Reviewed Domel families and Johnson U9825-001.

applicationMatrix.wcbAssessment: Brushless high-speed families are documented for this context, but the motor, controller, battery and fan must be qualified as one system.
applicationMatrix.basis: Nidec publishes V45, V55 and V65 cordless-vacuum motor modes; Domel publishes low-voltage brushless families.
applicationMatrix.limitations: No appliance-model or cross-supplier compatibility is established.
applicationMatrix.buyerAction: Approve voltage, controller, operating point, thermal path, acoustic target and mechanical envelope together.
applicationMatrix.evidence: Nidec and Domel explicitly name battery or cordless vacuum application contexts.

applicationMatrix.wcbAssessment: Both universal and selected brushless families may be relevant where the exact dry-use and regional electrical specification matches.
applicationMatrix.basis: Domel lists dry thru-flow and corded brushless families; IEC 60335-2-2 covers household vacuum appliance safety.
applicationMatrix.limitations: The standard is an appliance scope, not a motor approval or part listing.
applicationMatrix.buyerAction: Match regional supply, cooling path, insulation, protection and approved appliance documentation.
applicationMatrix.evidence: Domel and IEC publish the named family and appliance scopes.
applicationMatrix.scope: Household or similar use within cited sources.

applicationMatrix.wcbAssessment: Use only a family explicitly documented for the required wet/dry arrangement and validate the complete appliance safety design.
applicationMatrix.basis: Domel separates bypass dry/wet motors from dry thru-flow motors.
applicationMatrix.limitations: A bypass label by itself is not a wet-use approval.
applicationMatrix.buyerAction: Confirm water-ingress boundary, cooling route, discharge, seals, insulation and applicable commercial or household standard.
applicationMatrix.evidence: Domel publishes bypass motors for dry and wet applications with named construction variants.
applicationMatrix.scope: Domel product group; exact part and appliance validation remains required.

applicationMatrix.wcbAssessment: The U9825-001 documents one large-vacuum AC blower data set; it is a reference point, not a universal commercial specification.
applicationMatrix.basis: Johnson Electric names large vacuum cleaners as the application example.
applicationMatrix.limitations: Commercial wet/dry safety scope and site duty require separate validation.
applicationMatrix.buyerAction: Request the exact performance curve, duty, approval file, enclosure and service-part documentation.
applicationMatrix.evidence: Johnson Electric U9825-001 lists large vacuum cleaners as an application example.

applicationMatrix.wcbAssessment: A motor/fan family must be selected against the central system's duct resistance, cooling, duty and applicable method rather than a single peak number.
applicationMatrix.basis: ASTM F2105 includes household central vacuum motor/fan systems in scope.
applicationMatrix.limitations: The standard does not select a motor for a building or confirm a part.
applicationMatrix.buyerAction: Validate the complete system curve, duty cycle, enclosure, acoustic target, supply and approved part record.
applicationMatrix.evidence: ASTM F2105 includes household central vacuum cleaning motor/fan systems.

compatibilityChecks.requiredMatch: Manufacturer part number, suffix, revision, appliance model and serial range
compatibilityChecks.why: A family can contain materially different voltage, fan, control and interface variants.
compatibilityChecks.buyerAction: Use the current manufacturer parts list or service document; stop if identity is incomplete.
compatibilityChecks.evidence: Official Domel and Johnson material publishes series and exact model-level variants with different data.
compatibilityChecks.scope: WCB verification action based on reviewed variant structure.

compatibilityChecks.requiredMatch: AC/DC type, voltage, frequency, current, wiring, connector, controller signals and protection
compatibilityChecks.why: Brushless designs require electronic commutation and official families span multiple supply versions.
compatibilityChecks.buyerAction: Approve the wiring and control specification, not only the nominal wattage.
compatibilityChecks.evidence: Domel publishes battery and corded brushless versions; UL separates electronically protected motor requirements.
compatibilityChecks.scope: Family and standards boundary; no exact appliance fit stated.

compatibilityChecks.requiredMatch: Envelope, mounting pattern, orientation, shaft and fan assembly, discharge and connector clearance
compatibilityChecks.why: Published families differ by diameter, discharge and construction even when broadly similar.
compatibilityChecks.buyerAction: Compare controlled drawings and tolerances for the exact revision.
compatibilityChecks.evidence: Domel and Johnson publish different dimensional and construction fields.

compatibilityChecks.requiredMatch: Thru-flow or bypass path, fan stages, seals, duct interface, restriction range and wet/dry boundary
compatibilityChecks.why: Changing restriction or cooling route changes the operating point and thermal condition.
compatibilityChecks.buyerAction: Validate the complete appliance system curve and temperature under intended filter-loading and duty conditions.
compatibilityChecks.evidence: Domel separates thru-flow and bypass application groups; Johnson publishes performance at multiple restrictions.

compatibilityChecks.requiredMatch: Insulation, grounding, thermal or electronic protection, enclosure and applicable approvals
compatibilityChecks.why: A component change can invalidate appliance-level abnormal-operation or protection assumptions.
compatibilityChecks.buyerAction: Have qualified engineering and compliance personnel confirm the applicable standard and certification file.
compatibilityChecks.evidence: IEC 60335-2-2 covers vacuum-appliance safety; UL lists general, thermal and electronic motor protection standards.
compatibilityChecks.scope: Standards applicability only; no certification claim.

compatibilityChecks.requiredMatch: Operating curve, input, efficiency, speed, acoustic, vibration, duty and life-test condition
compatibilityChecks.why: Single-point peak data does not reproduce an application's working restriction or field duty.
compatibilityChecks.buyerAction: Request test data at the intended operating point and run appliance-level validation.
compatibilityChecks.evidence: ASTM F2105 defines motor/fan measurements under specified conditions; Johnson publishes restriction-specific data and a named life cycle.

possibleCauses: Brush or commutation system where applicable
failureModes.safetyBoundary: These are WCB inspection categories, not a remote diagnosis. Disconnect power and stored energy before authorized service.
failureModes.serviceAction: Confirm the exact wiring, protection state and approved diagnostic procedure before condemning the motor.
failureModes.evidence: Reviewed sources show materially different supply, control and protection boundaries across motor families.
failureModes.scope: WCB synthesis from published fields; exact fault cause is not disclosed by the sources.

failureModes.safetyBoundary: Do not infer a motor fault from an appliance symptom without isolating the system boundary.
failureModes.serviceAction: Measure against the authorized method and inspect filters, ducts, seals and fan path before substitution.
failureModes.evidence: ASTM and Johnson sources separate airflow, pressure and air power at defined points and restrictions.
failureModes.scope: WCB diagnostic framework; not a manufacturer fault tree.

failureModes.safetyBoundary: Repeated protection operation requires qualified service; bypassing thermal or electronic protection is unsafe.
failureModes.serviceAction: Verify cooling architecture, restriction, input, duty, insulation and protection against current documentation.
failureModes.evidence: Domel distinguishes cooling arrangements; UL publishes separate thermal and electronic protection standards; Johnson states operating temperature and life-test conditions.
failureModes.scope: WCB inspection categories derived from documented boundaries.

failureModes.safetyBoundary: Stop operation if contact, overheating or electrical hazard is suspected; do not disassemble outside authorized service.
failureModes.serviceAction: Inspect the approved mount, fan path and operating point and compare with manufacturer acoustic and vibration limits when available.
failureModes.evidence: Domel describes low-vibration brushless families; Nidec describes design changes for compact high-speed motors, but neither source provides a universal fault diagnosis.
failureModes.scope: WCB inspection categories; no exact cause is claimed.

representativeFamilies.scope: Nidec published case study; no current availability claim.

distinguishingSpecifications: Manufacturer publishes open, orifice and sealed data
representativeFamilies.evidence: Johnson Electric lists U9825-001 as a high-power, long-life AC blower with large vacuum cleaners as the application example.

procurementDecisions.attributeToVerify: Target system curve, input architecture, envelope, control, thermal path, duty, noise and compliance
procurementDecisions.comparisonTrap: Selecting from peak wattage or rpm
procurementDecisions.assessment: Shortlist by documented operating boundary, then validate the complete appliance.
procurementDecisions.basis: Official families show large differences in input, architecture and performance reporting.
procurementDecisions.limitations: Public family pages do not replace supplier-controlled drawings or qualification data.
procurementDecisions.buyerAction: Issue an engineering specification and request controlled drawings, curves, life data, compliance records and samples.
procurementDecisions.engineeringCheck: Run thermal, airflow, acoustic, endurance and abnormal-operation validation.
procurementDecisions.evidence: Reviewed manufacturer sources publish family-level selection variables; standards define separate performance and safety boundaries.
procurementDecisions.scope: WCB procurement method, not a supplier recommendation.

procurementDecisions.attributeToVerify: Exact approved part number, revision, model and serial range
procurementDecisions.comparisonTrap: Treating similar dimensions and wattage as equivalent
procurementDecisions.assessment: Use only current manufacturer service documentation or a formally approved engineering substitution.
procurementDecisions.basis: Family pages include multiple variants and omit appliance-specific approval relationships.
procurementDecisions.limitations: This profile cannot approve a replacement part.
procurementDecisions.buyerAction: Obtain the current parts list or written manufacturer confirmation before installation.
procurementDecisions.evidence: Published family and datasheet differences demonstrate why family identity is insufficient.

procurementDecisions.attributeToVerify: Controlled specifications, traceability, change control, test method and quality evidence
procurementDecisions.comparisonTrap: Accepting a brochure headline as production control
procurementDecisions.assessment: Qualify the supplier process and exact motor configuration, not only the product family.
procurementDecisions.basis: Manufacturer pages describe family breadth; measured results remain condition-specific.
procurementDecisions.limitations: No supplier audit or quality ranking is provided here.
procurementDecisions.buyerAction: Define approval samples, incoming controls, change notification and periodic performance checks.
procurementDecisions.evidence: Domel describes traceability and automated production for its brushless family; official standards define controlled test scopes.
procurementDecisions.scope: Domel claim plus WCB procurement synthesis.

procurementDecisions.attributeToVerify: Supply voltage, frequency, insulation, approvals, corded/battery architecture and appliance certification impact
procurementDecisions.comparisonTrap: Assuming a family name is electrically identical worldwide
procurementDecisions.assessment: Treat each regional electrical and compliance configuration as a separate approval item.
procurementDecisions.basis: Official families publish multiple voltage versions; IEC and UL cover different safety or protection boundaries.
procurementDecisions.limitations: Market access requirements depend on jurisdiction and final appliance.
procurementDecisions.buyerAction: Confirm regional configuration and certification file with qualified compliance personnel.
procurementDecisions.evidence: Domel lists multiple voltage versions, and IEC/UL identify applicable appliance and motor protection standards.
procurementDecisions.scope: Standards boundary; no legal market-access conclusion.

engineeringChecks.reason: Airflow and pressure move together with restriction; open and sealed values are endpoints, not one working condition.
engineeringChecks.buyerAction: Obtain the full curve and test in the actual duct, filter and nozzle system.
engineeringChecks.evidence: Johnson publishes multiple restriction points and ASTM defines motor/fan air-performance measurements.

engineeringChecks.reason: Supply and commutation architecture differ across AC universal, low-voltage BLDC and corded EC families.
engineeringChecks.buyerAction: Approve wiring, controller, firmware or signals, protection and EMC configuration for the exact variant.
engineeringChecks.evidence: Domel and Nidec publish multiple supply and brushless configurations.

engineeringChecks.reason: Thru-flow and bypass arrangements place cooling air in different system relationships.
engineeringChecks.buyerAction: Validate temperatures at clean and loaded-filter conditions across the intended duty cycle.
engineeringChecks.evidence: Domel separates thru-flow dry and bypass dry/wet product groups.

engineeringChecks.reason: Mount, fan, discharge, seals and connector clearance affect air leakage, vibration and assembly safety.
engineeringChecks.buyerAction: Use controlled drawings and tolerance analysis; validate sealing and vibration in the final assembly.
engineeringChecks.evidence: Reviewed families publish different diameters, discharge arrangements and connection details.

engineeringChecks.reason: A motor is integrated into an appliance with abnormal-operation, insulation, protection and use-scope requirements.
engineeringChecks.buyerAction: Have qualified compliance personnel assess the component change against the current appliance file and applicable standards.
engineeringChecks.evidence: IEC 60335-2-2 defines household vacuum-appliance safety scope; UL identifies motor and integral-control standards.
engineeringChecks.scope: Applicability reference only; not a certification statement.

standards.name: ASTM F2105-21
standards.jurisdiction: Test method published by ASTM International
standards.applicability: Measures suction, airflow, air power, maximum air power and input power for series-universal vacuum-cleaner motor/fan systems under specified conditions; it does not approve a replacement part.
standards.evidence: ASTM publishes the stated scope and significance.
standards.scope: Series-universal motor/fan systems in the standard.

standards.name: IEC 60335-2-2
standards.applicability: Covers electric vacuum cleaners and water-suction cleaning appliances within the stated household and similar-use voltage scope; applicability is to the appliance, not automatic motor certification.
standards.evidence: IEC publishes the 2026 scope for household and similar vacuum appliances.

standards.name: IEC 62885-2
standards.applicability: Covers performance measurement of mains-operated and cordless dry vacuum cleaners for household or similar use; it is a whole-appliance method, not a motor interchangeability rule.
standards.evidence: IEC publishes the 2026 scope and technical revision status.

standards.name: UL 1004 family
standards.jurisdiction: North American motor safety standards referenced by UL Solutions
standards.applicability: UL identifies general rotating-machine, thermally protected and electronically protected motor standards; the applicable evaluation depends on the exact motor and control design.
standards.evidence: UL Solutions lists UL 1004-1, UL 1004-3 and UL 1004-7 among standards for motors with integral controllers.
standards.scope: Standards overview only; no listed or recognized status is claimed for a profile family.

developments.title: IEC publishes the third edition of IEC 62885-2
developments.summary: The 2026 edition expands its stated scope to mains-operated and cordless dry vacuum cleaners and revises air-data and test-material organization.
developments.evidence: IEC's publication page lists the date, edition and significant technical changes.
developments.scope: Whole-appliance performance standard, not motor compatibility.

developments.title: Nidec documents a third-generation cordless vacuum motor lineup
developments.summary: Nidec states that its third generation used a resin housing and identifies V45, V55 and V65 modes with rated power outputs.
developments.evidence: Nidec's official case study provides the development narrative and lineup values.
developments.scope: Nidec case study; the page gives the year but not a precise release day.

developments.title: AMETEK combines DFS and Bison under the Bison business
developments.summary: AMETEK's announcement identifies Lamb vacuum motors among the combined business's product brands, preserving a current source trail for the historic Lamb name without adding a representative-family row lacking current public specifications.
developments.evidence: AMETEK's official announcement identifies the business combination and Lamb vacuum motors.
developments.scope: Corporate source identity only; no customer, OEM or exact product relationship.
